title: Judge rules Pentagon's risk designation against Anthropic was arbitrary and illegal - TCR 08/28/26
description:
A federal judge blocked the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a "supply-chain risk" in a 59-page ruling calling it unlawful First Amendment retaliation, Anthropic released the Model Hardware Standard, and QuEra reported that a Claude-built controller recovered its quantum laser system in 695 of 700 trials, and the U.S.
Army launched a five-vendor program worth up to $2.2 billion, aiming to deploy 20+ commercial nuclear microreactors and put power on a base by 2028.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-august-28-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:40 Federal court vacates the Pentagon's Anthropic ban
3:11 Anthropic's Model Hardware Standard and QuEra's self-healing controller
5:45 A hundred firms warn on AI cyberdefense
8:14 Meta's Project OT unravels
10:49 AI reads mammograms and sees heart disease
12:59 Close

This episode covers the federal court blocking the Pentagon-Anthropic blacklisting, Anthropic's Model Hardware Standard and QuEra's self-healing quantum controller, a 100-company cyberdefense warning alongside agents executing unowned llms.txt code inside Fortune 500 networks, Meta's shelved Project OT, which reportedly contemplated cuts of up to 60% for some teams, and a machine-learning model reading 97,364 mammograms to flag heart disease in women.

The through-line is the rulebook for the agentic era being written on three tables at once. A federal court blocked the Pentagon's retaliation against a lab that drew a military-use red line, affirming refusal as protected speech, while that same lab published an open standard letting agents operate physical and quantum hardware and QuEra used it to build a controller that fixes itself. More than a hundred rival firms signed a joint warning that AI-enabled attacks will outpace defenses within months, the same week researchers proved the point by claiming abandoned code that agents then phoned home from inside a Fortune 500 network. Meta ran the largest test yet of replacing workers with agents and read its own instruments honestly enough to stop when reported test figures showed code changes rising 220% but shipped features only 36%. And the infrastructure kept pace, with the Army anchoring a commercial microreactor market and a model reading routine mammograms to catch the heart disease that most often kills women.
